sentences.text: Before passing award I would like to mention certain facts which were happened before setting aside the previous award dated 25.08.2010.
Here in the present case, an award dated 25.08.2010 for an amount of Rs.3,07,393.75/ was passed by my Ld Predecessor against R.1 and R.2.
Thereafter the petitioner/DH has filed an execution petition for recovery of award amount.
Notice of the execution petitioner was issued to R.1 and R.2.
Meanwhile, respondent No.1 and 2 have filed an application U/O IX rule 13 CPC setting aside the award dt 25.08.2010.
During the arguments on the application U/O IX rule 13 CPC the petitioner/DH has given no objection if the application of R.1 and R.2 is allowed subject to deposit of 50% of the awarded amount.
On 09.11.2012 R.1 and R.2 have deposited a sum of Rs.2,00,000/ by way of draft and Rs.11,000/ in cash towards the costs.
Accordingly the judgment dated 25.08.2010 was set aside.

2. Vide this award I shall dispose of, the claim petition under Section 166 and 140 (old ) of The Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 being filed by petitioner, seeking compensation on account of damage of Union Of India vs Bageer Singh And Ors on 14 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/145815694/

sentences.text: Brief facts of the case are that on 21.11.1999 at about 10.15 P.M, Mewa Ram was driving the Army vehicle bearing registration No.BA No. 94 D 99570K, DCM Toyota.

When the traffic signal got green at Palam crossing near Palam Cinema and when he started to take right turn towards Mode line, suddenly a truck bearing No. DL1GB4311 being driven by R.1 hit the army vehicle from opposite directions after jumping the red light traffic signal.
As a result of this impact army vehicle was badly damaged.
The loss of damage was got assessed.
Thereafter present petition for claiming compensation was filed.

3), has filed the present petition and the petitioner claimed a sum of Rs. 11,30,422/ towards the losses/damages caused to the vehicle of the petitioner 5.

In the present case respondent No.1 and 2 have filed their joint WS stating therein that the offending vehicle alleged to have been involved in the accident was not responsible for the accident and no accident caused due to the rash and negligent driving of R.1.

sentences.text: 4 9 . I have heard Ld. counsel appearing on behalf of petitioner and Ld Counsel for respondents and perused the entire record.

My issue wise findings are as under:  ISSUE No. 1: Whether vehicle NO. BA No.94D99570K, DCM Toyota was damaged in road accident dated 21.11.1999 due to rash and negligent driving of R.1 and owned by R.2? OPP.
10.
The onus to prove this issue was upon the petitioner.
To prove this fact, petitioner has examined PW1.
He has deposed that on 21.11.1999 at about 10.15 P.M, he was driving the Army vehicle bearing registration No.BA No. 94 D 99570K, DCM Toyota.

When the traffic signal got green at Palam crossing near Palam Cinema and when he started to take right turn towards Mode line, suddenly a truck bearing No. DL1GB4311 being driven by R.1 hit the army vehicle from opposite directions after jumping the red light traffic signal.
As a result of this impact army vehicle was badly damaged.
PW 1 has duly been crossexamined.

But the testimony of PW1 with respect to accident and rash &
negligent driving of offending vehicle could not be shaken/impeached.
Even otherwise, the proof of negligence while disposing of a claim under MACT, is not that strict as it is under Section 279/337/338 of IPC.

The charge sheet was filed against MACT No. 76/2019 Union of India Vs Bageer Singh & ors Page No. 6 of 9 respondent no.1 and he has not filed any complaint against the police before any higher authority against such implication.

sentences.text: The evidence which has come on the file can be considered and becomes more relevant when there is no specific evidence led by other side in rebuttal.
It is admitted position by respondents No.1 and 2 that an accident was caused with the offending vehicle but it was caused due to negligence of Army vehicle.
But there is no evidence brought on record by the respondents to prove this defence.

11. This issue is decided in favour of the petitioner and against respondents by holding that Army vehicle bearing registration No.BA No. 94 D 99570K, DCM Toyota was damaged due to rash and negligent driving of truck bearing No. DL1GB4311 being driven by R.1 ISSUE NO.2: If issue No.1 is proved in affirmative whether the petitioners are entitled for any compensation , if yes , from whom and what amount ? OPP.
12.
Now come to the point whether claimants are entitled for compensation or not.
13. PW2 KGS Nair has proved the technical Inspector report of damaged vehicle vide Ex PW2/1.
He has proved the photographs of accidental vehicle vide Ex PW2/2.

He has deposed that Army vehicle was purchased in 1994 for sum of Rs.4,48,750/ and its value after depreciation, was Rs.3,36,562/
.
After the damage, its value was Rs.2,69,250/ plu 8.5% departmental charges ( CDA charges) the total amount was comes to Rs.3,07,393.75/.He has proved
the damaged assessed vide Ex PW2/3.
There is nothing on record to disbelieve the testimony of PW1 and PW2.
In view of the above discussion, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of MACT No. 76/2019 Union of India Vs Bageer Singh & ors Page No. 7 of 9 damages.

Having considered the submission of Ld Counsel for the insurance company and after going through Section 166 of Motor Vehicle Act 1988.

The Clause (3) of Section 166 was omitted by amended Act 53 of 1994 being effective from Union Of India vs Bageer Singh And Ors on 14 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/145815694/
5 14.11.1994.

sentences.text: Prior to amendment there was limitation of 6 months from the date of accident for filing claim.
But after amendment there was no limitation prescribed in the Motor Vehicle Act to file the claim and also at the time of filing present petition.
Moreover, Section 166 (3) of M.V Act which prescribed for the period of limitation was omitted vide Amendment No.53 of 1994.
Then Section 21 of the Limitation Act does not have any application qua limitation for filing a claim under Motor Vehicle Act.
So particularly considering the nature of M.V Act which is a benevolent Act.
A liberal approach should be exercised while granting compensation to the victim of accident.
The sole purpose of M.V Act is to grant a just and reasonable compensation to the victim of accident.
So the plea of Ld Counsel for the Insurance Company is not tenable qua granting interest to the claimant from the date of impleadment of insurance company.
15. Now coming to the extent of liability.
It has already been held herein above that damaged was caused to the vehihcle of petitioner due to rash and negligent driving of respondent no.1.
He is primarily liable to make payment.
However, the petitioners have made the respondent no. 3 (insurance company) as one of the party seeking direction to respondent no. 3 that it be directed to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
It is not in MACT No. 76/2019 Union of India Vs Bageer Singh & ors Page No. 8 of 9 dispute that the offending vehicle was not insured with the Respondent no.3 on the date of accident.

entities.text: MACT No. 76/2019 Union of India Vs Bageer Singh & ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Moreover, the evidence of the petitioner fully supports its case,
therefore, this issue is decided in favour of the petitioner and against respondents by holding that petitioners are entitled for compensation from Respondent no.3.

ISSUE No. 3 (RELIEF)
16.
Petition in hands is allowed.

Respondent no. 3 is directed to pay Rs.3,07,393.75/ to the petitioner, as compensation in this case alongwith interest @ 7.5% per annum for the date of filing of petition ie 02.09.2003 till the date of compliance i.e. 13.03.2024.
Thereafter interest @ 12% p.a for delayed payment.

The awarded amount shall remain as tax free in view of the judgment of Hon'ble High Court in case in R/Special Civil Application No.4800 of 2021 titled The Oriental Insurance Co Ltd Vs Chief Commissioner of Income Tax (TDS) decided on 05.04.2022.
17.

18. Respondent no.3 is directed to deposit entire amount of compensation with this tribunal, within 30 days from today, with an advance notice to petitioner.
19. File be consigned to record room.
